title: Best Places to Visit in October in India: The Complete 2026 Guide
summary: The best places to visit in October in India 2026: Rajasthan, Mysore Dasara, Goa beaches, Spiti Valley, Andaman Islands, Kerala backwaters and more with travel planning tips.
body_markdown:
October has no rival as India’s travel month. Not one of the best, the best. The monsoon withdraws from North India, Rajasthan, and the Deccan in early October, leaving clean air and comfortable temperatures. The Western Ghats are at their greenest. Andaman’s sea visibility returns after the monsoon months. Mysore hosts the most spectacular public festival in South India. And the calendar gives travellers four separate long weekend windows across the month, more than any other month in 2026.


## **Best Places to Visit in October in India: A Complete Overview**


This guide covers the best destinations across India for the month of October, organized by travel type and region. October 2026 has confirmed long weekends on October 2-4 (Gandhi Jayanti), October 17-20 (Dussehra with one day of leave), and October 24-26 (Valmiki Jayanti), in addition to a three-day window around Navratri on October 10-12. The destinations below are matched to October’s specific combination of post-monsoon freshness, festive energy, and increasingly comfortable temperatures across most of the country.


# **Best Places to Visit in October in India 2026: Region by Region**


## **Rajasthan: October Is the Beginning of the Best Season**


Rajasthan in October is in the transition from its hot and wet period into the dry, clear, and photogenic months of November through February. The October timing is specifically interesting because the landscape still holds some green from the monsoon, the lakes and reservoirs are full, and the crowds have not yet reached the levels that peak season brings.


**Jaipur** in October has the Amber Fort in the best light of the year. The late afternoon sun on the ochre sandstone, the Maota Lake below the fort still carrying its post-monsoon volume, and the walled city lanes before the full tourist-season rush. The weather is in the high twenties with cool evenings. For anyone planning a Rajasthan trip this year, October is a better month than November for photography and a comparable experience at considerably lower accommodation prices.


**Udaipur** in October has the lakes at their fullest. Lake Pichola and Fateh Sagar both hold their monsoon-filled levels into October, and the view from Monsoon Palace across a green-tinged Aravalli landscape with full lakes below is specific to this post-monsoon window. By December, the water levels have dropped and the landscape has browned. October catches Udaipur before that shift.


**Jodhpur** for the Mehrangarh Fort is strong in October for the same weather reasons. The blue-painted old city below the fort and the fort walls themselves photograph with particular clarity in October’s dry, low-humidity air.


**Best time within October:** The entire month works. Early October (first two weeks) retains more of the monsoon green. Late October is more consistently clear.


## **Mysore Dasara: The Most Spectacular Public Festival in South India**


Dussehra 2026 falls on Tuesday October 20, and Mysore’s version of this festival, called Dasara, is categorically different from how Dussehra is celebrated anywhere else in the country. For ten days leading up to Vijayadashami, the Mysore Palace is illuminated every night with 97,000 lights. The final day involves a grand procession through the city with the royal family, caparisoned elephants, and the image of Goddess Chamundeshwari in a golden howdah on the lead elephant.


The Mysore Dasara procession and the palace illumination during this period are among the most photographed events in India. The crowds are significant but manageable if you plan specific viewing positions in advance. The best viewing position for the Dasara procession is along the route between the palace and Bannimantap Grounds, and arrival 90 minutes early secures a clear position.


The long weekend around Dussehra, October 17-20 with one day of leave, is the natural planning window for a Mysore Dasara trip.


## **Goa: The Return of the Beach Season**


October is the transitional month in Goa. The first two weeks still carry some monsoon character: afternoon rain is possible, the sea can be rough, and watersports are limited. The last two weeks of October are when the tourist season properly begins: the beaches are emptying of the monsoon-season quiet, accommodation prices are still close to low-season rates, and the weather is moving toward the dry clarity of November.


The Dussehra long weekend of October 17-20 is often cited as the first major travel weekend to Goa in the festive season. The beaches at this time are not crowded in the December sense, the water is warming back up, and the Portuguese heritage of Panaji and Old Goa, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus and the Se Cathedral, are accessible without the full-season press of visitors.


The[Mumbai to Goa bus](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/mumbai-to-goa-bus-route) overnight makes the Gandhi Jayanti or Dussehra long weekend format clean from Mumbai.


## **Kerala: Backwaters and Hill Stations in Post-Monsoon Green**


Kerala in October sits in the tail of its southwest monsoon and is beginning to transition toward the northeast monsoon. The landscape is at its most intensely green, the waterfalls are still active, and the Alleppey backwaters carry their fullest water levels.


**Munnar** in October has the tea estate landscape in peak green and the Eravikulam National Park accessible. The waterfalls at Athirappilly are still at near-full flow. The temperatures in the Nilgiri foothills are in the low twenties.


**Alleppey (Alappuzha)** in October has the backwater canals full and the surrounding paddy fields green. Houseboat travel in this period gives the lush landscape version of the backwaters that the dry-season photos rarely capture.


The Onam harvest festival has passed by October, so the backwaters have the post-festive quiet that October specifically carries in Kerala.


## **Spiti Valley: The Last Reliable Window Before Snow**


The passes into Spiti Valley from the Manali side typically close in late October or November depending on annual snowfall patterns. October is the final month when the Rohtang Pass and the Kunzum La are reliably open, and Spiti in October has a specific character that no other month matches: the barley harvest is complete, the landscape is the grey-gold of harvested fields against grey granite, and the skies are the clearest of the year.


Travellers who have been considering Spiti but deferred should book October specifically. The weather window closes in November and the circuit is not accessible by road again until June the following year. The Delhi to Manali bus covers the approach corridor, with onward local transport into Spiti.


## **Andaman Islands: Visibility Returns After Monsoon**


The Andaman Sea has its lowest visibility during the monsoon months of May through September. October marks the return of clear water and the resumption of diving and snorkelling activities at their best. The sea condition in October is not yet at the January-March peak, but it is substantially better than anything from May onward.


Radhanagar Beach on Havelock Island, consistently ranked among Asia’s best beaches, is quiet enough in October to give you long stretches of near-empty sand despite being a well-known destination. Port Blair’s Cellular Jail and Corbyn’s Cove are accessible throughout, and the ferry services between the islands operate on regular schedules from October.


## **Coorg: Coffee Harvest Season**


October in Coorg is coffee harvest preparation season. The Arabica and Robusta estates across the Kodagu district begin the picking process in October and November, and visiting a working coffee estate at this time gives access to the agricultural process rather than just the visual landscape. The air has the specific quality of post-monsoon Ghats: cool, rich with forest smell, and misty in the early morning.


Abbey Falls is still at significant force in October. The Dubare Elephant Camp on the Cauvery River continues its morning interaction sessions. The drive from Bangalore through Mysore and into Madikeri has the greenest version of the Western Ghats road experience in October.


## **Practical Planning for October Travel**


October is one of India’s busiest travel months by booking volume. The long weekends in particular, especially Gandhi Jayanti (Oct 2-4) and Dussehra (Oct 17-20), fill buses and accommodation quickly. Booking two to three weeks ahead is the minimum for popular corridors during these windows.


For Mysore during Dasara specifically, accommodation within 15 km of the palace should be booked four to six weeks in advance. Hotel rooms within the city fill first.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Which are the best places to visit in October in India?**


The best places to visit in October in India include Rajasthan for post-monsoon clear weather (Jaipur, Udaipur, Jodhpur), Mysore for Dasara celebrations from October 11-20, Goa from the third week onward as the beach season begins, Kerala for backwaters and hill stations in peak green, Spiti Valley before the passes close, and Andaman Islands as sea visibility returns.


### **Is October a good time to visit Rajasthan?**


Yes, October is one of the best times to visit Rajasthan; the monsoon has cleared, temperatures are in the comfortable mid-to-high twenties, the lakes and reservoirs are still full from the rains, and the heritage sites are in better photographic light than the peak-winter months.


### **What festivals happen in October in India 2026?**


Major October 2026 festivals include Gandhi Jayanti on October 2, Sharad Navratri starting October 11, Dussehra on October 20 (with Mysore Dasara being the most spectacular version), and Valmiki Jayanti on October 26.


### **Is Goa good in October?**


The second half of October is good in Goa as the sea clears and the beach season begins; the first two weeks may still have afternoon rain; the Dussehra long weekend of October 17-20 is when most early-season Goa travel begins.
